title: Integration Risk Meter — mini deck (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This mini-deck is an operational sales enablement artifact geared at SEs and field sellers who need a fast, repeatable way to diagnose integration risk during discovery calls and pilot scoping. It’s intentionally lightweight: 8 slides, diagnostic checklist, quick scoring rubric, and two suggested fallback scripts.

Intended use (how to run it):
- 5–8 minute run during technical qualification or pilot kickoff.
- SE reads top-line questions to engineering buyer, then marks green/amber/red.
- Use aggregated score to recommend: hosted pilot, dedicated pilot, or private-onprem evaluation.
- Capture answers in pilot intake (JIRA: JIRA-GTM-792).

Slide 1 — Title + TL;DR
- Title: Integration Risk Meter — Quick Technical Diagnostic
- TL;DR speaker note: "This helps you close faster by matching deployment choice to actual integration friction. We aim to avoid overpromising a private on-prem pilot when a hosted + proxy cache will suffice."

Slide 2 — When to use this
- Use at first technical qualification (post-architect intro).
- Use before committing to a dedicated capacity conversation.
- Use when the prospect mentions regulatory/security/latency constraints.

Slide 3 — The 6 risk dimensions (one-line each)
- Data Residency & Compliance (Are there legal constraints on where model responses or logs can be stored?)
- Network Topology & Egress (Is the customer air-gapped, VPC-only, or using private peering?)
- Throughput & Latency Requirements (Peak qps and tail latency SLOs)
- Model Asset Controls (Do they require pinned model binaries, custom weights, or disallowed model families?)
- Observability & Tracing Needs (Do they require request-level traceability or token-level audit logs?)
- Change Management / Release Policy (Can they accept faster canaries or do they require strict internal approvals?)

Slide 4 — Scoring rubric (how to mark green/amber/red)
- Green = Low friction: standard hosted flows workable with minimal config.
- Amber = Moderate: likely need Dedicated or Private with some configuration (eg. VPC peering, dedicated GPU pool).
- Red = High: Private deployment or air-gapped onprem likely required.
- Quick note: score conservatively if multiple dims are amber.

Slide 5 — One-page checklist (copyable into notes)
- Data Residency & Compliance: Any contractual obligations (SOC/ISO/regulatory) that explicitly prohibit third-party hosted inference? (G/R/A)
- Network Topology: Can they open a port for an outbound-only TLS endpoint or require inbound-only? (G/R/A)
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target (ms) and whether model cold-starts are acceptable. (G/R/A)
- Throughput: Peak tokens / second estimate and burst patterns. (G/R/A)
- Model Controls: Do they need customers-supplied weights, custom fine-tuned models, or no-open-source-models policy? (G/R/A)
- Observability: Do they require token-level logs + retention policy? (G/R/A)
- Release cadence: internal change freeze windows, compliance approvals, or security gates? (G/R/A)
- Team readiness: Customer dev team size and prior experience hosting LLM endpoints? (G/R/A)

Slide 6 — Decision mapping (score -> recommendation)
- Mostly Green (0–1 amber, 0 red): Recommend Hosted pilot w/ API keys + caching + signed DPA.
- Mixed (2–3 amber, 0–1 red): Recommend Dedicated reserved capacity pilot + VPC peering and SLA.
- High friction (>=2 red or >3 amber): Recommend Private deployment evaluation; involve legal & infra early.

Slide 7 — Suggested scripts & fallback language (for seller/SE)
- Hosted-first path script:
  "From what you’ve described, the constraints look manageable with a hosted pilot using VPC peering and data masking. That will let you validate the integration in 2–3 weeks with minimal ops overhead."
- Private-first path script:
  "Given the regulatory constraints and network topology you described, we should scope a private deployment evaluation. That will take longer and needs legal + infra signoff; we’ll align SOW and timeline upfront."
- Quick fallback if unsure: "Let’s run a 1-week hosted smoke test on sanitized data while we scope the longer private evaluation — that reduces risk and gives us quick feedback."

Slide 8 — Operational next steps & owner map (who to loop)
- If hosted -> SE to create pilot intake, set retention window, enable prefix caching. Owner: SE (copy: solutions-eng).
- If dedicated -> Loop Solutions + Platform sales for reserved capacity quote. Owner: AE + SE.
- If private -> Loop Professional Services + Legal + Infra for network runbook and SOW. Owner: AE.

Appendix A — Quick scoring example (fictional)
- Prospect: Fintech payments platform
- Answers: Data residency (amber, needs EU-only), Network (amber, requires VPC peering), Latency (green), Model controls (red, cannot allow any 3rd-party-hosted model), Observability (amber) -> result = 3 amber + 1 red -> Recommend private deployment evaluation + concurrent hosted smoke test.

Appendix B — Open questions / TODOs (for this draft)
- Tune rubric thresholds for # of ambers -> currently conservative; validate with 10 closed pilots (owner: Ethan Park).
- Add short GDPR & PCI signal matrix for quick legal cues (owner: Maya Singh).
- Create a one-click Google Form to capture the checklist into JIRA automatically. (linked artifact: JIRA-GTM-792)

Notes for field testing and metrics
- Hypothesis: using the Meter reduces pilot scope creep by 30% and shortens time-to-first-data by 25%.
- Metrics to track: pilot conversion rate, pilot time-to-first-response, percentage of pilots that flip from hosted->private after kickoff.
- Data capture: require SE to attach completed checklist to pilot JIRA ticket.

Speaker-style rough notes (short)
- Lead: "This is not a vendor checklist; it’s an operational decision tool to match investment to actual friction. If we surface high friction early we save weeks of rework."
- When pushing back: "What level of risk would trigger your legal team to require an onprem evaluation?"

References and quick links
- Pilot intake ticket template: JIRA-GTM-792
- Internal kernel: confluence page CONFLUENCE-1254 (pilot scoping guide)
- Example SOW template: /legal/templates/pilot-sow-v2.docx (TODO: add link)

Author notes:
- Draft: iterate after 2 field tests. Keep lightweight — customer-facing PDF should be 4 slides only (TLDR + checklist + scripts + next steps).
- This doc intentionally mixes speaker notes and copy for slide text so SEs can copy/paste into a slide builder or notes app.

Unresolved decisions (for product/ops):
- Should we add an automatic recommendation in Console based on pilot intake fields? (Product question, tag: product-hosted-api)
- Can we automate retention defaults depending on the recommendation? (Ops/Legal)

End of mini-deck draft.

-- Sofia M. (notes)
